  ❌ You have to type skill names yourself in every future session here

questions.question:
D2 — Enable cross-project learnings search?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count fixture, branch main, reviewing PLAN.md.
ELI10: gstack keeps a local file of lessons learned per project. It can also search lessons from your other projects on this machine to spot patterns that apply here. Nothing leaves your machine either way. Solo developers usually want this on; people juggling multiple client codebases usually keep it off.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Off means missing a relevant lesson from another repo; on means a note from a client repo could surface in an unrelated one.
Recommendation: A because the search is local-only and the default for solo developers.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
A) Enable cross-project learnings (recommended)
  ✅ Findings from your other repos on this machine inform this review and future ones
  ✅ Stays local, no network, flip off any time with one config command
  ❌ Learnings from unrelated or client codebases can appear in this project's context
B) Keep learnings project-scoped
  ✅ Strict isolation between codebases, nothing from one repo shows up in another
  ✅ Still records and reuses this project's own learnings normally
  ❌ Patterns you already learned elsewhere have to be rediscovered here
Net: cross-pollination vs. strict per-repo isolation.

options.label: Enable cross-project (recommended)
options.description: gstack-config set cross_project_learnings true, then search with --cross-project.

options.label: Project-scoped only
options.description: gstack-config set cross_project_learnings false.

questions.question:
D5 — Which review posture for the rest of this CEO review?
Project/branch/task: main, PLAN.md "Add saved project views", approach B (spec-based views) selected.
ELI10: The mode sets how ambitious the rest of the review is. Expansion pushes scope up and recommends extras enthusiastically. Selective expansion keeps your scope as the baseline but shows each extra as its own yes/no so you cherry-pick. Hold scope only hardens what is already there. Reduction strips to the bare minimum. Whatever you pick, no scope changes without your explicit yes on each one.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Too ambitious and a small productivity feature grows into a platform project; too narrow and the obvious adjacent wins (default view, shareable link) get rebuilt later at higher cost.
Recommendation: SELECTIVE EXPANSION because this enhances an existing task list rather than building a greenfield feature, and approach B already opens a few cheap adjacent doors worth a look.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Net: how many adjacent opportunities you want to see before the rigor sections start.

options.label: SELECTIVE EXPANSION (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Plan scope stays the baseline and gets the full rigor pass
✅ Each expansion (default view, shareable link, shared views, etc.) is a separate neutral yes/no you control
❌ Adds several decision prompts before the deep review begins

options.label: SCOPE EXPANSION
options.description:
✅ Surfaces the 10x version and platonic ideal, recommended enthusiastically
✅ Best if you want saved views to become a real product pillar
❌ Risks turning a two-day feature into a multi-week views platform

options.label: HOLD SCOPE
options.description:
✅ Maximum rigor on exactly the four approach bullets, nothing else surfaced
✅ Fastest path to a bulletproof plan for the stated goal
❌ Cheap adjacent wins go unmentioned and may be rebuilt later

options.label: SCOPE REDUCTION
options.description:
✅ Finds the smallest shippable slice, useful if the pilot is really a demand test
✅ Minimizes new attack surface and migration risk
❌ Approach B already leans complete; cutting now would undo that choice

questions.question:
D6 — Proposal 1: Default view per member per project?
Project/branch/task: main, PLAN.md saved views, SCOPE EXPANSION opt-in ceremony (1 of 6).
ELI10: Imagine opening a project and the task list is already filtered the way you left it, no clicking required. Each member can mark one saved view as their default for a project; the list opens in that view, with a visible chip showing which view is active and a one-click way back to "All tasks". Concrete shape: a default_view_id on the project membership (or an is_default flag on saved_views with a unique partial index), read at task-list load. Effort: human ~half day / CC ~10 min.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Without it, members still start from the unfiltered list every session and reuse depends on remembering the picker exists, which is exactly how saved-filter features die.
Recommendation: Add because it turns saved views from a thing you remember to use into the thing you land on, which is the single biggest lever on the plan's reuse metric.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=5/10, C=0/10
Net: one flag and one load-time lookup buy the habit loop the pilot needs.

options.label: A) Add to this plan's scope (recommended)
options.description:
✅ Members land in their view automatically; reuse becomes passive instead of remembered
✅ Trivial schema: partial unique index on (member_id, project_id) where is_default
❌ Needs a clear "you're in a filtered view" indicator so newcomers aren't confused by missing tasks

options.label: B) Defer to TODOS.md
options.description:
✅ Keeps the first ship focused on save and reopen only
✅ Can be added later without a data migration if is_default is nullable
❌ Pilot measures reuse without the mechanism most likely to drive it

options.label: C) Skip
options.description:
✅ Smallest possible surface; no default-state confusion to design for
✅ Zero additional edge cases (deleted default view, etc.)
❌ Leaves the habit loop entirely to the user's memory

questions.question:
D3 — Which implementation approach should the plan commit to?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-H67mSL on main, PLAN.md saved project views.
ELI10: All three approaches let a member stop re-building filters, but they differ in how much of the future they leave open. A saves a blob of JSON per view and moves on. B first defines one shape for "what the list looks like right now" and uses that same shape for the URL, the saved view, and the remembered last filter. C skips naming entirely and just makes the URL and last-used memory do the work. The stakes: with an opaque blob, renaming a filter field later silently breaks every saved view pointing at it, and adding shared team views means a migration.
Stakes if we pick wrong: A ships fast but the first filter rename produces views that open blank with no error; C never meets the goal of named views.
Recommendation: B because one serialization is the DRY answer, stale views degrade visibly instead of silently, and sharing later is a column flip. The extra work is roughly 25 minutes of CC time.
Completeness: A=6/10, B=9/10, C=4/10
Net: about 25 extra minutes of CC time buys a schema that the URL, memory, and sharing can all reuse instead of three parallel state shapes.

options.label: B: ViewState schema (recommended)
options.description:
Completeness 9/10. Effort M (human ~4 days / CC ~45 min).
✅ One versioned ViewState shape drives URL params, saved views, and per-member last-used memory
✅ Loading a view validates against current filter vocabulary and shows a notice instead of a blank list
✅ visibility, is_default, and position columns mean sharing and defaults need no migration later
❌ More upfront schema design and a versioning story for the state column

options.label: A: Minimal table
options.description:
Completeness 6/10. Effort S (human ~2 days / CC ~20 min).
✅ Smallest diff that ships exactly what PLAN.md describes today
✅ Easy to reason about: one table, four endpoints, one dropdown
❌ Opaque JSONB means a renamed filter field breaks saved views silently with no user-facing error

options.label: C: URL + last-used only
options.description:
Completeness 4/10. Effort S (human ~1 day / CC ~15 min).
✅ No new table or endpoints, filters survive reload and are shareable by link immediately
✅ Lowest risk surface, nothing new to secure or migrate
❌ Does not deliver named, reopenable views, which is the stated goal of the plan

Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-H67mSL on main, PLAN.md saved project views, approach B chosen.

Selective expansion means I hold your scope as the baseline, make it bulletproof, and separately show you each add-on so you can cherry-pick with no sales pitch. Hold scope means no add-ons at all, just maximum rigor on what is written. Reduction means I cut the plan to the smallest thing that stops members re-building filters. questions.question:
D5 — Does the URL codec ship in this first release, or does it wait?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-H67mSL on main, saved project views, HOLD SCOPE, approach B.
ELI10: Approach B defines one ViewState shape and said the URL would use it too. Writing the current filters into the URL means reload and browser back keep your filters, and a copied link carries them. Named saved views work without it. In HOLD SCOPE my job is to flag any work that can wait without blocking the goal, and this is the one piece that qualifies. It is not new scope either way; it is sequencing of an already approved approach.
Stakes if we pick wrong: ship it now and the first release has one more surface to test; wait and the pilot has no shareable link, so members send screenshots instead.
Recommendation: A because the codec is the same serializer the API already needs, so the marginal cost is one encode/decode pair plus a router hook, roughly 10 minutes of CC time, and it removes the most common "lost my filters on reload" complaint the pilot would otherwise surface.
Completeness: A=10/10, B=7/10
Net: about 10 minutes of CC time now versus a known pilot complaint and a follow-up PR later.

options.label: A: Ship URL sync in v1 (recommended)
options.description:
Completeness 10/10. Effort S (human ~half day / CC ~10 min).
✅ Reload, back button, and copied links all preserve filters from day one of the pilot
✅ Same serializer as the API, so one codec is tested once and reused twice
✅ Page load has a clear precedence rule: URL state wins, then last-used view, then default
❌ One more surface to test: malformed or oversized URL state must degrade to the default list with a notice

options.label: B: Defer URL sync to follow-up
options.description:
Completeness 7/10. Effort S later (human ~half day / CC ~10 min).
✅ Smaller first release; picker and API are the only new surfaces to verify
✅ Pilot feedback can confirm whether link sharing is actually wanted
❌ Members lose filters on reload during the pilot, which is the exact pain the plan targets
